children: Chinese artificial-intelligence maker DeepSeek is releasing the engine that runs its AI models as open-source software.
The company on Tuesday released DeepInfer, which it described as its internal framework for inference, the process by which AI models take in and respond to prompts.

Though DeepSeek is known for releasing the weights to its models publicly, allowing anyone to download and run them, the move to also release its proprietary inference engine opens up a new avenue for the company to position itself as a cheaper alternative to AI services from U.S. firms.
"We're sharing our production stack to help the community lower compute costs, reduce energy use, and make AI more affordable," the company posted to X.
Right now, DeepInfer supports the company's DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model running on Nvidia or Huawei computing hardware.

The move also comes as the U.S. and China race to develop increasingly powerful AI models. The Homeland Security Department this week ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek AI technology from their systems and barred future purchases of the company's products and services.
